answer: Agents stake a bonded deposit of plume tokens to register, and each identity's weight is capped by a decaying onyx reputation score earned through verified peer attestations. Sybil attackers must fund many separate stakes and fake attestation histories, so the cost of minting N identities scales linearly while rewards stay flat, making the attack unprofitable. Honest agents accumulate sable-tier trust over epochs, and duplicate clusters are flagged when their attestation graphs overlap suspiciously.
